text: This spacecraft is so far away, a message you send it today arrives tomorrow.
On November eighteenth, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth.
And it's running out of power.
It's been flying since nineteen seventy-seven, on a computer with less memory than one photo on your phone.
Its radio is weaker than a fridge light bulb.
By the time that signal reaches us, it's a billionth of a billionth of a watt. Giant dishes still catch it.
But its power drops about four watts every year. So NASA keeps switching instruments off.
Only two science instruments are still on.
One day it'll go quiet, and keep flying anyway. So if you ever want to say goodbye, remember:
